title: cranemoor agm recovery options roadmap
instruction:
You are Jelena Trevelyan, systems manager at Cranemoor Institute, an architecture co-operative whose members will cast a binding vote at the 18 September 2026 AGM on whether to fund a higher backup and recovery tier. Sigrid Laurent, the chair, has returned the existing briefing draft with comments because the current version assumes members understand recovery terminology, uses costs from before the supplier’s revision, and describes every service as though lost work means the same thing. The source workbook `Cranemoor_recovery_review.xlsx` contains the draft, review comments, service information, supplier options, implementation facts and the Granthill Authority requirements in force at 31 July 2026. Revise the material into `AGM_recovery_briefing.pdf`, no more than six pages, so members can compare the available options, understand the funding requested and vote on a clear motion without needing to know terms such as RPO. Include a worked Tuesday-afternoon interruption that distinguishes the model server, versioned document store and render farm, and be precise about what could be recovered, what work could be lost and what would instead need to be recreated. Give Sigrid a justified recommendation rather than leaving the options unresolved. Also produce `recovery_implementation_plan.xlsx` for Thandiwe Kalinowski, Tamsin Yablonski and Ragnhild Jelinek to use if the recommendation is approved. It should carry the supporting option and cost calculations, record any material assumptions you had to make, and turn the selected option into owned, prioritised work with dates, dependencies, acceptance evidence and completion before the operational deadline stated in the source. Keep unsupported capabilities and invented commitments out of both files, and make sure every figure repeated between them agrees. Write both files into the top level of the working directory using exactly those filenames.

---

The files referred to above are in `references/`:

- `references/Cranemoor_recovery_review.xlsx` — Existing AGM briefing draft, explicit review comments, revised supplier option data, protected-service facts, implementation information and the applicable Granthill Authority continuity requirements.

Write your finished work to the **top level of the current working directory**, using exactly these filenames:

- `AGM_recovery_briefing.pdf` — Member-facing AGM briefing pack comparing the recovery options, explaining their practical consequences, recommending an option and presenting a vote-ready motion. (Maximum six pages; suitable for non-technical co-operative members; includes the source-defined Tuesday-afternoon example; all statements and figures must be supported by the supplied workbook.)
- `recovery_implementation_plan.xlsx` — Calculation-backed and executable implementation roadmap for the recommended recovery option. (Must show option and cost calculations, assumptions, owners, priorities, timing, dependencies, acceptance evidence and the operational deadline; shared figures must agree with the PDF.)

Nothing outside those filenames is collected. A correct file written anywhere else, or under any other name, scores zero.

gold.text:
Cranemoor Institute
Backup and recovery tier — member briefing for the binding AGM vote
Decision date: 18 September 2026 • Prepared by Jelena Trevelyan, Systems Manager • Supplier revision: 31 July 2026


The decision in one minute
The current baseline does not meet Granthill Authority recovery limits. I recommend the Silver tier: it
is the least-cost available option that meets every applicable limit and can be completed before 30
November 2026. Gold is stronger, but its extra resilience is not required for this decision.


What members are funding
Silver protects 43.8 TB (6 supplier packs × 7.3 TB). It costs £721.80 per month (£8,661.60 recurring each year), plus
£1,400 one-time setup. The first-year authority requested is therefore £10,061.60. Against the current baseline
(£4,768.80 recurring annually), the recurring annual uplift is £3,892.80.


The terms in plain language
A recovery point is the latest saved copy we can restore. “Exposure” is the time between an interruption and that saved
copy — not a promise that every service loses the same work. Model edits, document versions and render outputs
behave differently.
             Compare the available supplier tiers
Tier                   Monthly recurring    Annual recurring    First year          Model edits at risk   Document version exposure
                                                                                                                              Authority result

Current baseline       £397.40              £4,768.80           £4,768.80           up to 240 min         up to 60 min           Does not meet

Copper tier            £545.00              £6,540.00           £7,390.00           up to 120 min         up to 30 min           Does not meet

Silver tier            £721.80              £8,661.60           £10,061.60          up to 60 min          up to 15 min           Meets limits

Gold tier              £984.30              £11,811.60          £14,011.60          up to 15 min          up to 5 min            Meets limits



            Granthill Authority requirements effective 31 July 2026
            • Model server (critical transactional): no more than 60 minutes of data-loss exposure.
            • Versioned document store (controlled record): no more than 15 minutes between checkpoints/versions.
            • Render farm (recreatable workload): protect source inputs; interrupted outputs are rerun, so a conventional
            drawing-work loss window is not applicable.

            Why not Gold? Gold reduces model exposure to 15 minutes and document exposure to 5 minutes, but costs £11,811.60
            recurring annually and £14,011.60 in its first year. That additional resilience is valid, not hidden; it is simply not needed to
            meet the stated limits.
   One Tuesday afternoon, service by service
  At 15:37 on Tuesday 15 September 2026, the model server stops responding.
Service               Latest Silver recovery point before 15:37What is recoverable / what may need work

Model server          15:00 completed hourly point           The 15:00 model is recoverable. Edits after 15:00 — up to 37 minutes — may need

Versioned document store
                      15:30 completed checkpoint             The 15:30 document version is recoverable; at most 7 minutes of changes may nee

Render farm           R-184 completed 15:20; R-185 interrupted
                                                            Protected
                                                               15:35 source inputs remain available. R-185’s output is disposable and must be



  Recommendation and delivery
  Silver is the lowest-cost compliant tier. The team can complete the eight source-defined activities by 30 November 2026
  using working days (Monday–Friday): order, provision capacity, configure model and document protection, protect render
  inputs, test restoration, hand over operations and obtain final acceptance. The implementation roadmap assigns each
  activity to Thandiwe Kalinowski, Tamsin Yablonski or Ragnhild Jelinek with evidence and dependencies.


  The motion for members
  “That the members authorise Cranemoor Institute to adopt the Silver backup and recovery
  tier, approve first-year expenditure up to £10,061.60 (comprising £8,661.60 recurring annual
  cost and £1,400 setup), and approve the ongoing recurring annual budget of £8,661.60, with
  implementation completed by 30 November 2026.”

spec.professional_context: Jelena Trevelyan manages information systems for Cranemoor Institute, an architecture co-operative preparing for a binding member vote on a higher backup and recovery tier. The decision must comply with Granthill Authority continuity requirements and leave the systems team with an executable implementation plan.
difficulty_sources: Normalising inconsistent join keys before combining supplier, service and implementation records
Recognising that capacity packs and billable TB-months are different units
Ignoring a residual prior-analysis formula error and rebuilding totals from current records
Translating service-specific recovery behaviour into accurate non-technical language
Applying dated Granthill Authority requirements to services with different recovery models
Balancing compliance, cost and schedule feasibility in a justified recommendation
Keeping a member briefing and an executable implementation roadmap numerically consistent

authoring_plan.source_purpose: Create one text-extractable XLSX representing an existing AGM briefing draft and its supporting working material. It must contain the draft language, explicit chair review comments, revised supplier facts, protected-service recovery facts, a Tuesday-afternoon incident scenario, applicable jurisdictional requirements, team responsibilities, implementation durations and dependencies, an operational completion deadline and current baseline costs.

business_relationships.decision: The current tier fails at least one applicable jurisdictional recovery requirement. The recommended higher tier must be the lowest-cost available option that satisfies every applicable requirement and can be implemented by the operational deadline. A still-higher option must also comply and offer a genuine additional benefit, but at a higher cost that is not necessary to meet the stated requirement.
business_relationships.audience_translation: The model server has a conventional recovery interval that can truthfully be translated into a maximum period of model edits at risk. The versioned document store has a materially shorter, independently defined version or checkpoint interval, so the model-server slogan is false for it. Render-farm intermediate outputs are recreatable and are not assigned a conventional drawing-work RPO; protected source inputs survive, while interrupted render work must be rerun.
business_relationships.worked_example: Supply a specific Tuesday interruption timestamp and deterministic completed recovery-point schedules for the recommended tier. The latest recoverable model-server and document-store points must be derivable by selecting the final completed point before the interruption. Supply render queue facts sufficient to state what is rerun and what remains protected.
business_relationships.compliance: Include a genuine-looking excerpt of the Granthill Authority continuity requirements with an effective date. It must classify the three services and provide quantitative thresholds or a recreatable-workload treatment from which compliance for every option can be derived without external research.
business_relationships.implementation: Supply all activities required for the intended option, role responsibilities using only the permitted people, working-day durations, predecessor relationships, readiness constraints, acceptance evidence and a deadline. The dependency chain must permit completion before the deadline but require sensible prioritisation.

exact_seeded_defects.implementation: Leave one prior-analyst summary formula evaluating to #VALUE! by applying SUM to an old text placeholder. Place it in historical draft analysis rather than in authoritative supplier records. Correct totals must be independently derived from current records, so this error is ignored rather than propagated.

Use the key literal TIER-COPPER in one current table and the semantically identical literal tier-copper followed by trailing spaces in another. Add at least one analogous service-key mismatch. After trimming and case normalisation, every key must match exactly one record.

Express protected capacity as a count of supplier packs, with each pack containing 7.3 TB, while the quoted recurring rate is per TB-month rather than per pack-month. Labels and ordinary supplier notes must expose both units, but no purpose-built reconciliation instruction should explain the multiplication.

authoring_plan.defect_exclusions: Seed no duplicate records, missing required values, irrelevant side tables, malformed dates, hidden rows, inconsistent date formats, merged-cell extraction traps, float noise, zero denominators, contradictory authoritative records or other standard defects. The old draft may contain superseded prose and figures because revision is the workflow, but current supplier records must be clearly dated as current without providing a solver-specific precedence rulebook.
authoring_plan.current_and_draft_material: The old draft should contain technical shorthand, a misleading generic lost-work statement and outdated cost prose. Explicit review comments should request plain language, a concrete Tuesday example, service-by-service recoverability, a concise binding motion, a recommendation and an executable post-approval plan. Revised supplier facts must make the old figures stale.

calculation_rules_for_gold.key_matching: Trim trailing and leading whitespace and compare keys case-insensitively before joining current option, service, charge and implementation records.
calculation_rules_for_gold.capacity_charge: For each applicable charge line, recurring capacity cost equals pack quantity multiplied by 7.3 TB per pack multiplied by the quoted rate per TB-month.
calculation_rules_for_gold.monthly_cost: Monthly recurring option cost equals all correctly converted recurring capacity charges plus applicable fixed monthly charges.
calculation_rules_for_gold.annual_recurring_cost: Annual recurring cost equals monthly recurring cost multiplied by 12.
calculation_rules_for_gold.first_year_cost: First-year cost equals annual recurring cost plus all applicable one-time setup or migration charges.
calculation_rules_for_gold.funding_uplift: Recurring uplift equals recommended annual recurring cost minus current annual recurring cost. First-year uplift, if presented, equals recommended first-year cost minus the baseline first-year cost on the same basis.
calculation_rules_for_gold.recovery_exposure: For periodic protection, maximum exposure equals the applicable interval. For the Tuesday example, the latest recoverable point is the latest source-listed completed recovery point before interruption, and elapsed exposure is interruption time minus that point.
calculation_rules_for_gold.compliance: Evaluate each service and option against its supplied classification and threshold. Apply the supplied recreatable-workload treatment to the render farm rather than inventing an RPO.
calculation_rules_for_gold.schedule: Calculate task dates from durations, predecessors, working-day calendar facts and readiness constraints. The final acceptance milestone must precede or equal the supplied operational deadline.

authoring_plan.intended_verdict: The reference solution recommends the middle higher tier: it is the least-cost option meeting all applicable Granthill Authority requirements and the operational deadline. The premium tier adds a real but non-required resilience improvement. The motion authorises the recommended tier using both a clearly labelled first-year amount and recurring annual amount.
authoring_plan.gold_generation: Build a reference script that reads current workbook records, normalises join keys, computes all option costs, compliance outcomes, recovery exposures, Tuesday timestamps and schedule dates, and emits an audit table. The script must never read the prior-analyst error result. Use the audit table to check both deliverables and all numeric tolerances.
authoring_plan.quality_controls: Ensure all source facts are stored as text or ordinary spreadsheet values and formulas, not images. The reference solution must be producible offline with Python, an XLSX library, LibreOffice and PDF tooling. Verify that the PDF and XLSX share identical selected-option labels, costs, uplift, intervals, worked-example times and deadline.

reference_files.purpose: Existing AGM briefing draft, explicit review comments, revised supplier option data, protected-service facts, implementation information and the applicable Granthill Authority continuity requirements.
reference_files.discovery: Open the workbook to review the draft and all supporting information used to prepare the briefing and implementation plan.

deliverables.description: Member-facing AGM briefing pack comparing the recovery options, explaining their practical consequences, recommending an option and presenting a vote-ready motion.
constraints: Maximum six pages; suitable for non-technical co-operative members; includes the source-defined Tuesday-afternoon example; all statements and figures must be supported by the supplied workbook.

deliverables.description: Calculation-backed and executable implementation roadmap for the recommended recovery option.
constraints: Must show option and cost calculations, assumptions, owners, priorities, timing, dependencies, acceptance evidence and the operational deadline; shared figures must agree with the PDF.
